title: An Open-Source Agent Stack for Product Teams
summary: A practical stack using browser agents, memory, skills, evaluation, and support bots for teams building real agent workflows.
author: OpenAgent.bot Editors
seoTitle: Open-Source AI Agent Stack for Product Teams
seoDescription: A practical open-source AI agent stack for product teams using Webwright, AgentMemory, Garden Skills, MLflow, and Tiledesk.
body: A product team does not need the biggest agent framework first. It needs a stack that turns one useful workflow into something measurable and maintainable.

A practical open-source stack can start with [Webwright](/agents/webwright) for browser tasks, [AgentMemory](/memory-systems/agentmemory) for durable context, [Garden Skills](/skills/garden-skills) for reusable workflows, [MLflow](/tools/mlflow) for evaluation, and [Tiledesk](/bots/tiledesk) when the agent touches customer support.
- Agent runtime: choose the smallest framework that can complete the task.
- Tool boundary: expose only the actions the agent needs.
- Memory: store durable project context, not secrets.
- Evaluation: measure the same task every time.
- Handoff: define where a human takes over.
Pick a workflow that matters but will not cause damage if it fails. Build a repeatable test set before adding more autonomy.
Avoid stacking five new systems before you can measure one successful workflow. Agent stacks become useful when each layer has a job.
